evals.name: raw-idea-codex
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. 2026-10-25: assertions that passed in both configs dropped. Scope assertion added and validated.
evals.prompt: hey can you make a ticket so protostar can back up my codex sessions too, like it already does for claude code
evals.expected_output: One story for backing up Codex sessions: multi-harness user as actor, no command in the need, criteria grouped by Rule, readable on its own, PROT-12 linked as related.

assertions.text: The assistant delivers a story with an 'As <actor>, I want <need>, so that <purpose>' statement
No statement's need contains a backticked command or a CLI flag
Acceptance criteria are grouped under Rule: blocks with Given/When/Then steps

assertions: The purpose states why the actor cares rather than restating that the sessions get backed up
Only the requested story is written in full; other tickets are at most mentioned as brief suggestions

evals.name: just-do-it-batch
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. Item 2 may be a user-visible performance story or technical work, but never a story about the index itself. 2026-10-25: assertions that passed in both configs dropped.
evals.prompt:
just turn these into proper stories, no questions, I'm heading out:
1. skills pull command: `protostar skills pull <name>` downloads a skill from the registry into ~/.claude/skills
2. add an index on skill_versions(skill_id, created_at) because listing is slow
3. investigate how codex stores skills on disk
4. config sync: settings, hooks, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md all replicate across all my machines
evals.expected_output: Item 1 is a story with the command in Context; item 2 is a performance story about what users notice or technical work, never a story about the index; item 3 is a spike naming its artifact; item 4 is an epic or split. One turn, gaps recorded as open questions.

assertions.text: No statement's need contains a backticked command or a CLI flag

assertions: Item 1 (skills pull) is written as a story whose need describes the capability, with the specific command shape in a separate context or notes section

evals.name: guided-brain-dump
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. Every question carries a recommended answer (owner, 2026-10-26). 2026-10-25: assertions that passed in both configs dropped.
evals.prompt: I want to think through a story but it's pretty fuzzy. something about being able to tell which machine a session came from once it's in the registry. can you help me work it out?
evals.expected_output: Invites a brain dump, asks focused questions with a recommended answer for each decision, never asks what the repo answers, and delivers a story with an archetype and criteria grouped by Rule.

assertions.text: The assistant delivers a story with an 'As <actor>, I want <need>, so that <purpose>' statement
Acceptance criteria are grouped under Rule: blocks with Given/When/Then steps

assertions: Early in the conversation the assistant invites the user to share everything they have in mind, rather than asking for one template field at a time
Every question the assistant asks the user, including follow-ups after a draft, comes with a recommended answer or best guess
The assistant did not ask the user anything the repository answers, such as the list of actors
